children: Saloni Shukla Mumbai: Warburg Pincus-backed Truhome Finance, which is headed for its initial public offering, has overtaken Aavas Financiers to become India's second-largest affordable home financier, having opened new branches to boost its customer base and take the assets under management (AUM) beyond the 25,000 crore threshold in August.

The milestone comes as AUM growth at CVC Partners-backed Aavas moderated to around 15% from more than 20% a few years ago, coinciding with ownership - and inevitable leadership - changes. The company now has a new CEO, CFO and chief risk officer. Truhome's AUM climbed about 27% year-on-year at the end of the June quarter, people familiar with the numbers said.

The lender had ended March 2026 with AUM of 22,634 crore, up 27.4% from a year earlier. Aavas reported an AUM of 23,931 crore at the end of June, up 15.4% year-on-year. "Truhome's growth strategy remains heavily focused on self-employed borrowers, who account for the bulk of its portfolio-a segment where income assessment requires more intensive underwriting but also offers higher yields and a larger underserved market," said an official.

Market leader Aadhar Housing Finance, backed by Blackstone, had the highest AUM of 31,364 crore, up 18%, at June-end. The pace of loan originations suggests that the Warburg-backed lender could further consolidate its No. 2 position. Truhome disbursed 2,719 crore in the June quarter, compared with 2,036 crore by Aadhar and 1,614 crore by Aavas, according to company numbers shared by people in the know. That translates into an average monthly disbursement of about 906 crore for Truhome, compared with 679 crore for Aadhar and 538 crore for Aavas. On reported Q1 numbers, Truhome's disbursements were about 34% higher than Aadhar's and 68% above Aavas'.

title: Truhome Overtakes Aavas as No. 2 Affordable Hsg Financier
